To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
economic and cultural threats have different effects on anti-immigrant sentiment and that the effects of these threats vary across countries and over time.

(1) economic threat is a more significant determinant of anti-immigrant attitudes in economically depressed countries, while cultural threat is a more important determinant in economically prosperous countries; (2) economic threat is more significant among the unemployed than the employed; (3) economic threat is stronger among the lower class than among the higher class; and (4) cultural threat is more significant in the context of high immigration than in the context of low immigration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of perceived group threats that underlie anti-immigrant sentiment across Europe.
the nature of perceived threat and its effects on anti-immigrant sentiment in a comparative European context.
the question of why anti-immigrant sentiment varies across time and across countries in Europe and what factors explain this variation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the economic crisis has not yet affected the level of perceived threat in Europe, but the crisis has affected its nature.

economic and cultural factors, as well as their interaction with structural factors, are important in understanding the variable nature of anti-immigrant attitudes in Europe, and that the economic crisis has not yet had a significant impact on these attitudes.

economic conditions, in particular the unemployment rate and the economic crisis, have the strongest effect on anti-immigrant sentiment, while cultural threat, as measured in this article, does not have a significant influence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
economic and cultural foundations vary across time and space and are not always in a direct relation with one another.
anti-immigrant sentiment is a complex phenomenon that varies over time and space.
the more immigrants there are in a country, the higher the threat of competition for jobs and the more negative the attitudes toward immigrants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the economic crisis may lead to more anti-immigrant sentiment, but this will be mediated by the nature of the economic crisis, the political climate and the nature of the immigration.
anti-immigrant sentiments are not a fixed phenomenon but rather are shaped by the economic, social and political context.
anti-immigrant sentiments vary across different countries and over time.
